newsitem.title: USA: Rite Aid to buy two drug store chains - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Rite Aid to buy two drug store chains - WSJ.

text.p: Rite Aid Corp has agreed to buy two closely held drug store chains in Alabama and Louisiana, The Wall Street Journal said.
In Monday's electronic edition, the paper cited a person close to the company saying the purchase price of the two transactions will total between $325 and $340 million.
The deal would give the drug store chain an additional 332 stores and a presence in southern markets, the story said.

The chains targeted are K&B Services Inc of New Orleans, which operates 186 stores and had 1996 revenue of $580 million, and Harrison Co's Harco Drug of Alabama, with 146 stores and 1996 sales of $258 million, the story said.
